tasks.short: Observe freight loading and procedure compliance

steps.what: Read actual loading procedures and shipment context using native shipment and procedure-version filters
inputs: Actual shipment record and current loading procedures
outputs: Verified loading context and procedure references in the freight inspection system

steps.what: Observe actual freight loading and crew actions to determine whether the actual procedures are followed; capture observed facts
outputs: Actual loading observations and observed compliance concerns

steps.what: Write and check the actual required loading-observation entry using native reuse of the verified shipment identifier
Save the actual entry in the same inspection workspace

tasks.design: Use native shipment and procedure views in the freight inspection system, {OPS_SYSTEM}, with current procedures in {DOCS}. Retain actual loading observation and separately write the real observation entry, reusing only the shipment identifier.
tasks.previous_blocker: Procedure context is repeatedly located and shipment identifiers recopied into real inspection entries.
tasks.enabler_now: Native views and record context can reduce clerical handling.
tasks.still_hard: Actual crew actions and changing loading conditions require direct observation.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when practice differs from the actual required procedure.

ambition.what: No additional inspection coverage or automated crew evaluation is assumed.

build_days.consent_and_access: 1-3 to inspect actual shipment and inspection access

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native shipment views and identifier reuse can reduce clerical handling while freight loading observation remains human.

assumptions: Representative loading observation with an actual required inspection entry. Shipment and procedure owners produce existing records during ordinary work; focal reading and verification remain in s1. Crew loading work remains actual unchanged work, not a source of claimed saving.

s2 counts actual observation and fact capture. s3 separately counts required writing and all checking. Only the exact identifier verified in s1 is reused; there is no clean visual feed or automatic worker-compliance decision.
Use native features first; existing views and identifiers yield no new gain. If no entry is actually required, remove it and measure the real episode rather than inventing a report.

Any actual stop instruction, violation notice or remedial recommendation requires its real separate work and authority. No such action is hidden in observation or saving. Ordinary save is ungated with no author self-approval or saving.

Provisional shares ignore the prior. Gross 10*0.20+9*0.10=2.9; upkeep 1 leaves net 1.9. Retained s1-s3 labour is 96.1 already counted. Save share 1 is the integer minimum for negligible effort, fully retained.
unknowns: Existing procedure views and shipment defaults
research_questions: Observe one loading inspection and separate direct observation from actual written records and any actual notices.

already_counted.description: Procedure reading, actual loading observation and required entry writing and checking remain in s1-s3.

incremental.description: Maintain shipment and procedure views beyond ordinary inspection checks.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Upper bound requires repeated procedure navigation and identifier copying. Existing native views and context leave no additional gain or new upkeep. Actual observation remains fully retained.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Read actual inspection findings and relevant procedures using native case and procedure-reference filters
outputs: Verified violation evidence and exact references

steps.what: Recommend actual remedial procedures to correct violations found during inspections, considering the evidence, feasibility and limits of authority
inputs: Original current procedures and actual operating constraints

steps.what: Write and check the actual recommendation entry using native reuse of exact violation and procedure references
Save the recommendation entry in its existing workspace
Actually explain the remedial recommendation and unresolved concerns to the internal operations supervisor in the normal spoken handoff

tasks.design: Use native case and procedure references in {OPS_SYSTEM} and {DOCS}. The inspector determines the actual remedy, writes its record and separately gives the real spoken recommendation to operations.
tasks.previous_blocker: Exact case and procedure references are repeatedly located and recopied into recommendation records.
tasks.enabler_now: Native views and reference reuse can reduce that repeated handling.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing an appropriate correction and explaining limits require inspection expertise.
tasks.human_edge: Recommend a practical response that fits the actual violation evidence.

ambition.what: No automatic remedy, work instruction or compliance clearance is assumed.

build_days.consent_and_access: 1-3 to inspect actual case and procedure access

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native case and procedure references can assist recommendation records while choosing and explaining remedies remain human.

assumptions: Representative recommendation episode with a real written entry and spoken internal handoff. Inspectors produce original findings and procedure owners current procedures during ordinary work; focal reading and verification are counted in s1, actual remedy selection in s2.

s3 separately counts actual writing and all checking; only verified references from s1 are reused. No clean violation classification, free transcript or automatic remedy selection is assumed. Missing evidence returns to actual investigation.

Use native features first; existing views and links have no new gain. No recommendation report is invented after a purely informal conversation; if the actual episode has no entry, remove it and re-estimate.

s5 is actual spoken advice, not a hidden written send or binding instruction. Actual formal notices, stop orders, remedial work and clearance require their real work and authority if included. Ordinary same-system save is ungated with no author self-approval or saving.

Provisional shares ignore the prior. Gross 20*0.10+29*0.20=7.8; upkeep 2 leaves net 5.8. Retained s1,s2,s3,s5 labour is 91.2 already counted. Save share 1 is the integer minimum for negligible effort, fully retained.
unknowns: Actual written and spoken recommendation channels
research_questions: Trace one real remedial recommendation from violation evidence to its written entry and actual handoff.

already_counted.description: Evidence reading, actual remedy judgement, recommendation writing and real spoken handoff remain in s1,s2,s3,s5.

incremental.description: Maintain case and procedure links beyond ordinary recommendation checking.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Upper bound needs repeated case navigation and reference copying. If native records already handle both, no additional saving or new upkeep is incurred. Remedy judgement and the actual recommendation conversation remain unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Inspect cargo and handling devices for compliance

steps.what: Read actual cargo records, handling-device history and applicable current requirements using native shipment and equipment filters
outputs: Verified cargo, device and requirement references

steps.what: Inspect actual loaded or lashed cargo, storage cargo and handling devices; capture actual observed conditions and defects
inputs: Actual cargo, lashings, storage location and handling devices
outputs: Actual observed cargo and device conditions and notes

steps.what: Determine actual compliance with health and safety requirements and the need for maintenance from original inspection evidence
outputs: Human inspection findings and maintenance-need judgement

steps.what: Write and check the actual inspection entry using native reuse of verified cargo and handling-device identifiers
Save the inspection entry in the same inspection workspace

tasks.design: Use native cargo and device views in the freight inspection system, {OPS_SYSTEM}, with original requirements in {DOCS}. Keep physical inspection and actual compliance judgement human, then write the real inspection entry separately.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requirement context and existing cargo or device identifiers are repeatedly located and copied.
tasks.enabler_now: Native views and record context can reduce these clerical operations.
tasks.still_hard: Cargo condition, lashings and device defects require actual inspection and judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise conditions that a record does not describe and determine actual maintenance need.

ambition.what: No automated clearance or extra physical inspection capacity is assumed.

build_days.consent_and_access: 1-3 to inspect actual cargo and equipment record access

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native cargo and equipment views can reduce record handling while physical inspection and compliance judgement remain human.

assumptions: Representative physical cargo-and-device inspection with an actual inspection entry. Cargo and maintenance staff produce original records and procedure owners current requirements during ordinary work; focal reading and verification remain in s1.

s2 counts all actual observation and note capture, s3 actual compliance and maintenance judgement, and s4 the separate real record writing and checking. Only exact identifiers verified in s1 are reused. No clean visual or defect feed is assumed.

Use native features first; existing views and identifier context give no new gain. Missing records or mismatched identifiers require manual investigation. Do not invent an extra report after inspection if none is required.

The finding does not release cargo, authorise equipment use, issue a violation notice or order maintenance. Actual formal actions require their real work, authority and distinct steps if included. Ordinary same-system save is ungated with no author self-approval or saving.

Provisional shares ignore the prior. Gross 20*0.10+9*0.10=2.9; upkeep 1 leaves net 1.9. Retained s1-s4 labour is 96.1 already counted. Save share 1 is the minimum integer representation of negligible effort, fully retained.
unknowns: Actual inspection record and clearance process
Existing cargo and device context views
research_questions: Observe a real cargo inspection and distinguish source lookup, physical inspection, judgement, entry and actual formal actions.

already_counted.description: Source reading, actual cargo inspection, compliance judgement and real inspection writing and checking remain in s1-s4.

incremental.description: Maintain native inspection views and identifiers beyond ordinary inspection checks.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Upper bound requires repeated lookup and exact identifier entry. Existing native tools that already remove both leave no additional saving or new upkeep. Physical inspection and compliance judgement remain fully retained.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Notify workers about special shipment treatment

steps.what: Read the actual shipment documents and current treatment requirements using native shipment-reference filters
inputs: Actual shipment information from the shipper
outputs: Verified shipment context and exact source references

steps.what: Determine what actual special treatment must be communicated for this shipment and clarify uncertainties against the original instructions
outputs: Human interpretation of the actual required treatment and unresolved questions

steps.what: Write and check the actual internal shipment-handling entry using native reuse of exact shipment and instruction references
Save the handling entry in the same workspace without dispatching a message
Actually notify the internal shipment workers in the on-site spoken briefing of the special treatment required and clarify their questions
outputs: Actual spoken worker notification and clarification

tasks.design: Use native shipment views in {OPS_SYSTEM} and original treatment sources in {DOCS}. The inspector determines the actual information, separately writes the handling entry and gives the real on-site notification to the workers.
tasks.previous_blocker: Shipment and treatment references are repeatedly found and recopied around actual worker briefings.
tasks.enabler_now: Native views and exact reference reuse can reduce repeated handling without inferring a treatment.
tasks.still_hard: Correct treatment interpretation and clear communication to actual workers require human attention.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise ambiguity and verify workers understand the actual shipment requirement.

ambition.what: No autonomous treatment instruction or extra shipment capacity is assumed.

build_days.consent_and_access: 1-3 to inspect actual treatment sources and notification channels

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native shipment views and exact reference reuse can assist handling records while actual treatment interpretation and spoken notification remain human.

assumptions: Representative actual internal on-site briefing with a real handling entry, not every notification channel. Shippers supply actual shipment information and responsible instruction owners current treatment requirements in ordinary work; focal reading and interpretation are counted in s1-s2.

s3 separately counts the actual handling record and all checking; only references verified in s1 are reused. No clean treatment classification, free transcript or automatic instruction generation is assumed. Missing or uncertain information requires manual clarification before the briefing.

s4 is an ordinary same-system save, not the notification. Notifications are disabled for that save. s5 is the actual spoken worker notification, fully retained. If actual notification uses a written message or external send, add its completed exact version, real authority and separate gated action rather than applying this spoken episode unchanged.

Do not invent a handling entry if the actual process only uses existing original instructions; remove it and measure the real work. Use native features first; existing views and reference links carry no new gain. Actual physical special treatment remains workers' unchanged work, not a claimed saving.

Provisional shares ignore the prior. Gross 25*0.10+14*0.10=3.9; upkeep 1 leaves net 2.9. Retained s1,s2,s3,s5 labour is 95.1 already counted. Save share 1 is the integer minimum for negligible active effort, fully retained, ungated and carries no saving or author self-approval.
unknowns: Actual spoken versus written notification mix
research_questions: Trace one actual special-treatment notification from original shipment sources to any handling entry and actual worker handoff.

already_counted.description: Source reading, actual treatment interpretation, handling writing and real spoken worker notification remain in s1,s2,s3,s5.

incremental.description: Maintain shipment views and treatment-reference reuse beyond ordinary handling checks.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Upper bound needs repeated source navigation and reference copying. If native shipment views already cover s1 navigation, only 1.4 copying points remain eligible; 1 upkeep leaves 0.4. Actual worker notification remains unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

reach: Freight crews and shipment workers performing actual handling
Operations supervisors receiving real remedial recommendations
Shippers and procedure owners producing original information
skills_to_grow: Direct observation and evidence-based compliance judgement
Exact shipment and equipment reference discipline
Clear actual worker notification and record boundaries
role.ambitious_version: A transportation inspector who handles existing records efficiently while retaining physical inspection, remedial judgement and direct communication with workers.
